text.p: Caterpillar Inc said Tuesday it expects 1997 profits to be higher than 1996, based in sales that it expects to be "moderately" higher.
Earnings per share for the year are expected to be "moderately higher," reflecting the benefit of the compnay's share repurchase program, the heavy equipment maker said.
The outlook is a switch from January, when the company forecast 1997 profits near 1996 levels of $1.4 billion or $7.07 a share.
The company reported $16.52 billion in sales in 1996.
But the company also warned that the 1997 forecast could be affected by greater than expected Federal Reserve tightening and lingering weakness in European demand.
Also, if the dollar remains overvalued versus the yen, price erosion will likely occur, Caterpillar said.

Caterpillar noted that the economic and industry outlook improved from January because the United States and Canada are now expected to have better economic growth and higher machine industry demand than originally anticipated.
The company said it expected U.S. gross domestic product to grow by three percent in 1997, up from the two percent it expected earlier.
The company said the Federal Reserve is likely to raise interest rates further before year-end to preempt any increase in inflation.

While expecting wordlwide machine industry demand (excluding the Commonwealth of Independent States) to be slightly better than last year, demand for engines is seen near 1996 levels, Caterpillar said.
Lower demand for truck engines should be offset by higher demand for other commercial engines, while demand for turbines is expected to meet or exceed last year's levels.

In Europe, the economy is forecast to pick up due to low interest rates and favorable currencies, but the risk is increasing that this growth may not occur soon enough to offset the impact of tight fiscal policies in the construction industry, Caterpillar said.
In Japan, tight fiscal policies will depress economic growth, making any improvement in Japan industry demand unlikely, Caterpillar said.

But excellent growth in developing parts of Asia and faster growth in Latin America should lead to higher industry demand, Caterpillar said. In the CIS, the Russian economy is expected to be weaker than expected, with little or no growth now forecast for the year, Caterpillar said.
Caterpillar shares were up one at 80-3/8 Tuesday.
